source.title: Hybrid Switching Optimization Strategy for Efficient Training of Deep Neural Networks on the MNIST Dataset

record.file_problem: Full article text is present. It contains a few apparent editing or formatting inconsistencies, including a mismatch between the stated venue year and the issue date.
record.tranche_reason: Compares Adam, SGD, and an Adam-to-SGD hybrid on MNIST and reports test accuracy and test loss, a different intervention and measure from the claim versions' specified studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimizer-comparison outcomes on MNIST, which bear on V4. It does not report random-label fitting, width sweeps, convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparisons, large-batch comparisons, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Its statement that SGD tends to generalize better appears as background; it is not an independently tested result.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares Adam, SGD, and Adam-to-SGD switching using held-out MNIST accuracy and loss across five learning rates. These results test V4, including its switching provision, despite the short training budget.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the authors' intended conclusion: epoch-based switching combines Adam's early convergence with SGD refinement and can improve MNIST performance, with the highest reported accuracy, 98.02%, at learning rate 0.002. Their broader claim of superior performance across learning rates overstates Table III, where switching loses to SGD at 0.01 and Adam at 0.0001. The conclusion's statement about highest test loss is an apparent wording error.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates a hybrid Adam-to-SGD-with-momentum training recipe against Adam and SGD on MNIST; it does not test the broad optimizer comparisons or training-test gap measures in the original versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate changes which optimizer performs best; Hybrid leads at 0.002, 0.001 and 0.0005, SGD leads at 0.01, and Adam leads at 0.0001 by test accuracy.
record.problems: Only MNIST and a fully connected network are evaluated, for 10 epochs, with three initializations and averages but no variability estimates. Table III gives test metrics, not paired training and test error. The results therefore do not directly measure the training-test gap. Abstract mentions FCN, CNN and LSTM, while the methods/results describe a fully connected model.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out performance.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed to interpolate.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.

Language benchmarks, other adaptive optimizers, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, and equal or better adaptive-method training performance. No numerical paired training/test results establish a generalization-gap comparison.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations to large-batch training.
Dropout interventions and interactions with training-set size, augmentation, or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparison with alternative measures.

record.verdict_notes: All table values are correctly transcribed. Subjects are optimizers applied to the same network, rather than distinct model architectures. Each row combines accuracy and minimum test loss and should be split if one measure per row is required. Results average three initializations without reported spread. Comparing each optimizer's best reported accuracy gives SGD 97.76% and Adam 97.65%, a small difference with unknown uncertainty. The paper explicitly emphasizes short-budget convergence rather than best attainable generalization. Table IV reaggregates the recorded losses and introduces no independent result; its Adam minimum and range omit the 0.0785 entry without changing its stated minimum. PCA trajectories and qualitative claims about flatter minima do not measure V7.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Network-width sweep beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

No language benchmarks; no broad adaptive-optimizer family comparison; no broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, or switching ablation. The paper's optimizer comparison is on MNIST with a fully connected network and a stated range of learning rates.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptive large-batch recipes.
Dropout comparisons and interactions with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the training-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.

relationships.condition: MNIST fully connected network, 10 epochs, learning rate 0.01
relationships.reason: SGD exceeds Adam in accuracy, 97.76% versus 92.03%, and has lower test loss, 0.0690 versus 0.2632 (R1, R3).
relationships.display_finding: Reported accuracy was higher and test loss lower for SGD than Adam, but the comparison remains unverified.

relationships.condition: MNIST fully connected network, 10 epochs, learning rates 0.002, 0.001, 0.0001, and 0.0005
relationships.reason: Adam outperforms SGD on both held-out measures at all four rates; the optimizer ranking depends on learning rate under this short budget (R5–R6, R8–R10, R12, R14–R15).
relationships.display_finding: Reported Adam advantages over SGD on both held-out measures at all four rates remain unverified.

relationships.reason: Switching improves Adam's accuracy from 92.03% to 94.41%, but remains below SGD's 97.76%, showing incomplete recovery (R1–R3).
relationships.display_finding: Reported switching gains over Adam remain unverified; at 0.002 and 0.001, Adam already outperformed SGD.

relationships.reason: Switching improves accuracy over Adam by only 0.37–0.43 percentage points, with lower test loss; these modest gains lack variability estimates (R4–R5, R7–R8, R13–R14).
relationships.display_finding: Reported small accuracy gains and lower test loss relative to Adam remain unverified and lack variability estimates.

relationships.reason: Switching worsens Adam's accuracy from 96.22% to 95.71% and increases test loss from 0.1192 to 0.1388, so its benefit depends on learning rate (R10–R11).
relationships.display_finding: Reported lower accuracy and higher test loss after switching remain unverified.

reader_labels.condition: MNIST fully connected network, tested learning rates
reader_labels.reason: Hybrid is not consistently best: it underperforms SGD at 0.01 and Adam at 0.0001; at the other reported rates it has the best test accuracy and loss (R1–R15). The comparison is limited to this benchmark and brief training setup.
